title: The divided soul of the British right
gist: A first-hand report from two 2026 London right-wing conferences (ARC and the inaugural CPAC Great Britain) argues the British right has split into a 'reconstruction' faction that sees itself defending institutions and a Trumpian 'burn it down' faction that treats Britain as already lost. Both camps are almost entirely devoid of policy on the economy, energy, health and defence, leaving Reform UK and the Conservatives ideologically loud but governmentally unprepared as the electoral right fragments three ways.

themes.theme: Three-way fragmentation of the right-of-centre vote

insights.claim: The UK right-of-centre vote is now split three ways between the Conservatives, Reform UK and Restore Britain, with Reform leading polls but slipping as Nigel Farage faces scrutiny over his finances and Andy Burnham enters Downing Street.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: A fragmented right raises the probability of prolonged hung-parliament dynamics and policy discontinuity risk for UK-exposed assets and gilt markets.
insights.quote: The electoral landscape has fragmented, with the Conservatives, Reform UK and Restore Britain all now competing for right-of-centre votes.
insights.locator: I went to ARC—and the inaugural CPAC

insights.claim: Rupert Lowe has absorbed a chunk of Nigel Farage's most radical supporters by appealing to declinist sentiment on X, constraining Farage's ability to moderate toward the centre.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: Farage is squeezed: moving to the centre costs him his base, staying radical costs him urban seats — a key swing factor in UK election pricing.
insights.quote: On his right, Rupert Lowe has hoovered up some of his most radical supporters, largely by appealing to declinist sentiment on X.
insights.locator: The person for whom this question is most pertinent

insights.claim: Any British party seriously contending for government must win urban seats where voters are angry about deteriorating public services but not about neighbourhood diversity or urban vibrancy, making anti-London rhetoric electorally self-defeating.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: Watch the London mayoral race as the cleanest test of whether populist city-bashing has an electoral ceiling.
insights.quote: They are upset about deteriorating public services, but not by the diversity of their neighbours nor the vibrancy of urban life.
insights.locator: any party seriously contending for government

themes.theme: Reconstruction vs demolition: the ARC/CPAC split

insights.claim: The ARC conference frames right-wing politics as a rearguard defence of tradition against progressive invaders, explicitly inverting the left's framing that populist conservatism is the radical departure from liberal democratic norms.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: Understanding which self-image dominates predicts whether a future right-wing government tries to capture institutions or dismantle them.
insights.quote: We are the defenders, Kruger argued; they are the invaders scaling the castle walls.
insights.locator: This is how the ARC speakers see their political project

insights.claim: The CPAC Great Britain crowd treats the left's cultural hegemony as so total that the country is already lost, abandoning the 'rebuild' project in favour of war on 'the blob' and the 'deep state'.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: A demolition-minded governing right implies higher institutional and regulatory volatility than a restorationist one.
insights.quote: These people didn’t appear to be trying to “rebuild” anything; the left’s supposed cultural hegemony is so total that the country itself is already completely lost.
insights.locator: What was said onstage, however

insights.claim: Australian journalist Paul Kelly's distinction between a 'Churchillian' and a 'Trumpian' right is the most useful axis for reading British conservatism, with ARC still tilting toward the former and CPAC firmly in the latter camp.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: A portable taxonomy for classifying right-wing movements across the Anglosphere by their attitude to existing institutions.
insights.quote: Australian journalist Paul Kelly distinguished between the “Churchillian” and “Trumpian” right in attendance, with the balance of support tilting toward the former.
insights.locator: For instance, at last year’s ARC conference

insights.claim: British conservatives are now genuinely uncertain whether there is anything left worth conserving, an unresolved question that makes their programme incoherent rather than merely radical.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: Ideological incoherence at the top of a likely-winning coalition is a leading indicator of policy reversal risk after an election.
insights.quote: Conservatives appear uncertain about whether there is anything left to conserve, or whether they have given up on much of the west as it now exists.
insights.locator: The division between those who call for “reconstruction”

themes.theme: Foreign policy as the live fault line

insights.claim: Support for Ukraine against Russia is the clearest dividing line between the two British right factions, with most of the ARC network remaining pro-Ukraine and Trump-adjacent speakers in the minority there.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: UK defence-spending and Ukraine-aid continuity depends on which faction controls a future right-wing government — relevant to European defence contractors.
insights.quote: most of the ARC tribe remain supportive of Ukraine in its defensive war against Russia
insights.locator: One evident difference between them is on foreign policy

insights.claim: Roughly a third of attendees at CPAC Great Britain were American, and visiting US figures such as Jack Posobiec and Matt Schlapp openly prescribed a Trumpian revolution and looser gun laws for Britain.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: US movement politics is being actively exported into UK party formation, importing American polarisation dynamics into UK political risk.
insights.quote: around a third of them were American anyway
insights.locator: Compared to the stark white of ARC’s interiors

themes.theme: Climate denial colliding with physical reality

insights.claim: The right's professed defence of facts over groupthink does not extend to scientific consensus on climate change or vaccination, with vaccine sceptic Eric Metaxas given a prime ARC speaking slot.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: Signals that climate and public-health policy would be reversed, not merely slowed, under this coalition — a tail risk for UK renewables project pipelines.
insights.quote: This supposed defence of facts over groupthink did not extend, of course, to the scientific consensuses on climate change and vaccinations.
insights.locator: This supposed defence of facts over groupthink

insights.claim: Nigel Farage mocked the UK's official red weather alert on the hottest June day on record, a day when London Ambulance Service logged a 50 per cent increase in immediately life-threatening calls and an estimated 2,124 UK deaths were later linked to that week's heatwave.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: Quantifies the growing gap between populist climate rhetoric and measurable heat mortality — a widening political liability as extreme heat recurs.
insights.quote: It would later be estimated that 2,124 deaths across the UK were linked to that week’s heatwave.
insights.locator: Conversely, Nigel Farage kicked off his interview

insights.claim: Two years after the Conservatives' electoral defeat, the British right's parties have developed almost no policy agenda beyond reducing migration and abandoning net zero.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: A policy-empty opposition means an incoming right-wing government would improvise, raising the variance of fiscal and regulatory outcomes.
insights.quote: these parties have largely focused on taking cheap shots at the hapless Keir Starmer and have thought little about their own policy agenda beyond reducing migration and abandoning net zero
insights.locator: I didn’t get definitive answers to these questions

insights.claim: Neither the ARC nor the CPAC conference produced meaningful content on the economy, cost of living, healthcare, transport, taxation, social care or defence — the cost of living being voters' top stated concern.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: The gap between the electorate's top concern and the right's agenda is an exploitable vulnerability that could reprice UK election odds.
insights.quote: On healthcare, transport, taxation, social care? Crickets.
insights.locator: Finally, these competing narrative frames

insights.claim: The nearest thing to a new policy idea at ARC was family-based taxation replacing individual income tax, with a 25 per cent income tax and student debt discount per child for mothers, plus removal of emissions-based penalties on larger family vehicles.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: Pro-natalist tax restructuring is the one concrete fiscal proposal circulating on the British right — watch for it entering manifestos with revenue implications.
insights.quote: removing emissions-based penalties on larger family vehicles
insights.locator: About the closest ARC got to a new idea

insights.claim: On energy the British right's only articulated positions were Farage boasting about approaching South Korean nuclear engineers and generalised attacks on Ed Miliband's green agenda.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: South Korean nuclear vendors are the named beneficiary of a Reform-led energy policy; UK offshore wind and net-zero-linked subsidies are the named casualty.
insights.quote: Farage boasted about calling in South Korea’s nuclear engineers
insights.locator: On energy

insights.claim: Labour's failure in office stemmed from entering government without adequate preparation, and the British right shows no sign of heeding that lesson despite being best placed to win the next election.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: Repeat of the unprepared-government pattern implies another cycle of policy churn and weak execution risk for UK-domestic equities.
insights.quote: As his adviser Morgan McSweeney recently acknowledged, Labour did not adequately prepare for power.
insights.locator: A bare policy chest and a muddle sense of direction

themes.theme: Money, media and tech behind the movement

insights.claim: ARC's co-founder and major funder Paul Marshall simultaneously owns the Spectator and Unherd and part-owns GB News, concentrating the British right's intellectual infrastructure in one financier.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: A single-owner media stack means UK right-wing narrative shifts can be tracked through one balance sheet.
insights.quote: ARC’s co-founder and one of its major funders is Paul Marshall, the evangelical financier who owns the Spectator and Unherd, and part-owns GB News.
insights.locator: Having drawn breath in the gallery space

insights.claim: Executives from Palantir and Anduril held a private, journalist-excluded dinner alongside the ARC conference even as the conference's own book preached Tolkienian temperance toward technology.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: Defence-tech firms are cultivating the British political right directly — a channel to watch for UK procurement and surveillance contracts.
insights.quote: Executives from tech companies Palantir and Anduril, for instance, held a private dinner at the Lincoln’s Inn alongside the conference. Journalists were excluded.
insights.locator: It was a brave assertion

insights.claim: The ARC conference's stated civilisational priorities — mass deportations, transgender issues, wokeness — track the trending topics of Elon Musk's X rather than any independent policy analysis, suggesting the platform's algorithm is setting the right's agenda.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: Political agendas set by engagement algorithms are unstable and hard to price; watch X trends as a leading indicator of right-wing policy noise.
insights.quote: The key talking points onstage—mass deportations, “transgenderism”, wokeness—could have been lifted from the “trending” section of X.com.
insights.locator: It is ironic, because at ARC

insights.claim: CPAC Great Britain was a logistical and attendance failure — the room peaked at half full and was mostly two-thirds empty, speakers including Ron DeSantis pulled out late, and a youth ambassador publicly criticised the organisation.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: The Trumpian wing of the British right has loud online reach but thin real-world organisational capacity — a reason to discount its near-term electoral threat.
insights.quote: The conference room peaked at about half full, and for most of the conference it was around two-thirds empty.
insights.locator: The problem for Liz Truss

insights.claim: The British right's cryptocurrency enthusiasm surfaces at its populist wing rather than its institutionalist one, with CPAC running a dedicated 'crypto day' featuring shameless boosterism at which Farage chose to speak.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Clark
insights.so_what: UK crypto-friendly regulation is politically coupled to the Trumpian faction, not the conservative mainstream — a factional bet, not a consensus one.
insights.quote: perhaps unwisely at CPAC, he spoke on “crypto day”
insights.locator: The person for whom this question is most pertinent
